leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer Kane, Mele and Molenkamp for time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect. They share the same three laureates and the case that a testable Z2 prediction was confirmed in HgTe quantum wells and has been stable for roughly two decades. They differ on weight: Danielsson, whose opening first choice was B043, and Pearce, whose opening first choice was B002, moved to B004 after reading the other ballots, while Eriksson and Johansson ranked it first at opening. Citation wording differs. Danielsson would anchor it on the Z2 theory and the first experimental observation, and Johansson wants it kept narrow to the quantum spin Hall effect so that three-dimensional work is not drawn in. All four record the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 2016 overlap as real reservations, not as disqualifying ones.

Three members prefer Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock and its development to 10^-18. They share the two-name allocation, which they call the cleanest on the shortlist, independent reproduction across laboratories, and the argument that the magic-wavelength lattice is a new architecture and not a refinement. They differ on how to present the lineage objection. Kroll and Lindroth treat the 2005 and 2012 prizes as answerable and want the citation anchored on the lattice concept. Olsson names continuity as the main objection the committee must answer, and moved from B012 to B006 after the opening round. Kroll discloses a Hall-laboratory connection and Olsson a Tokyo and JSPS link, which are not shared by the other two supporters.

One member, Mehlig, prefers Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero for magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. The case is a quantitative prediction followed by the 2018 discovery of correlated and superconducting states, framed around flat-band physics and not the pairing mechanism. Mehlig names B004 as a first alternative and accepts that B004 is safer on maturity. Other members list B009 as a first or second alternative but hold it back because the mechanism is debated and the field is young; Johansson ranked it fourth for that reason.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members ranked B004 in the opening round and seven placed it in their top three. In round 1 every member who does not prefer B004 still lists it as a first or second alternative, and no member argues against its scientific standing.

B004, B006 and B009 each have a stable three-, two- and three-name laureate set across every member who proposed them, so the disagreement among them is about merit, maturity and credit, not about who the laureates would be.

Interpretive stability is accepted as a strength of both B004 and B006. B006 has been reproduced across several national laboratories, and B004 has about two decades of transport and ARPES confirmation.

No member defends the Higgs candidate B002 as ready on attribution, including its original proposer Pearce, who moved away from it because of the collaboration-credit problem, and no member prefers B015, B023, B032 or B012 in round 1.

IceCube (B043) is respected as a new messenger channel, but the diffuse flux is firmly established while source identification is thin and credit sits inside a very large collaboration, so members treat it as not yet ready as a first choice.
scientific_disputes: Whether lattice clocks are a new concept (Katori's magic-wavelength trapping, many-atom operation at 10^-18, as argued by Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson) or an incremental precision step within the lineage of the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for ion-based control (raised by Mehlig, Pearce and Eriksson, and with less weight by Danielsson and Johansson).

Whether the Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall effect are a new organising principle distinct from the 2016 topological phase prize (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth) or risk looking like a return to the same theme (raised by Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson and Pearce as a reservation, and by Mehlig as a reason to weigh B009 higher).

Whether conceptual reach (B004, B009) should outweigh demonstrated, deployed measurement capability (B006), and whether the pending redefinition of the second is a reason to prefer B006 now or to wait, as Pearce suggests.

Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene is a question about a derived phase and not the discovery (Mehlig) or a reason to defer B009 (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce).
attribution_disputes: For B004, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route that Molenkamp's group tested, and none is credited; Zhang is deceased. Seven of the eight round-1 files raise this point. Members differ on whether it is disqualifying: Kroll and Olsson say they would not oppose B004 if the committee accepts the boundary, Mehlig says it is his main reason not to rank B004 first, and Pearce wants it stated openly in the record. Three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Hasan, Shen) also lies outside the credited names.

For B006, credit may leak towards ion-clock groups (for example Al+) and other lattice-clock laboratories at NIST, PTB, SYRTE and Tokyo, and Ye's place relative to the comb lineage was raised by Johansson. Supporters regard this as a boundary-of-credit question and not a reason to doubt Katori and Ye.

For B009, Yuan Cao and other experimental co-authors and parallel groups are outside the credited set, so the experimental half rests on Jarillo-Herrero alone; Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson raise this.

For B002, four names (Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) compete for three seats. The opening proposals differ: Eriksson, Kroll and Pearce proposed Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee, while Johansson proposed Gianotti, Della Negra and Virdee. For B043, the credited pair of Halzen and Spiering sits inside a collaboration of thousands, with DUMAND and Baikal predecessors outside the pair.
maturity_disputes: B009 is judged young by most members: the decisive experiments are seven to eight years old, the pairing mechanism is debated, and twist-angle disorder and strain complicate the intrinsic phenomenology. Mehlig argues that waiting for a mechanism may mean waiting indefinitely, and Lindroth notes that an early award cannot easily be corrected.
B043 source identification (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane) rests on few associations at moderate significance, and KM3NeT results may change the picture.
B006 is mature and reproduced, but the redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, so some of its practical impact is still prospective.
B004 is treated by all members as mature, so the dispute there is about overlap with the 2016 prize and not about confirmation.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson-goran directs WACQT at Chalmers and collaborates with Delsing, Wilson and Kockum, and would recuse himself from deliberating on B015 (circuit quantum electrodynamics).

Kroll-stefan documents a research stay in John Hall's laboratory during his doctoral period, from which Ye's career emerged, and asks whether this calls for recusal on B006; Lindroth does not think recusal is needed on that basis alone.

Olsson-eva works in electron microscopy and cannot claim independence on B012 (Rose, Haider, Krivanek), and has a University of Tokyo fellowship, a JSPS fellowship and long exchanges with Japanese universities, with Katori at the University of Tokyo; she knows of no collaboration with Katori or Ye but asks the committee to judge recusal on B006.

Pearce-mark, the chair, records a PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and balloon polarimetry background close to B043 (IceCube) but no documented membership of the IceCube collaboration, and notes it as a possible bias and not a formal recusal issue.
questions_for_round2: For B004: is a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp citation defensible without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and can wording limited to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect and its first observation (as Johansson and Kroll suggest) answer the credit gap and the 2016 overlap, or must the committee treat the omission as disqualifying?

For B004 versus B006: should conceptual novelty or demonstrated metrological reach and clean attribution carry more weight, and can supporters of B006 state specifically what the lattice clock adds beyond the 2005 and 2012 prizes in a citation that would not claim the comb or ion-clock lineages?

For B006: do the Kroll and Olsson disclosures require recusal or a separate check of Ye's credit relative to the comb lineage, and does any ion-clock or other lattice-clock group have a claim that makes the Katori-Ye pair look incomplete?

For B009: can a citation framed around flat-band prediction and the first observation of correlated and superconducting states be separated from the open pairing mechanism, and is the committee prepared to credit the experiment to Jarillo-Herrero alone, without Cao and others?

Is there a principle for choosing among founders and spokespersons in B002, and for the IceCube pair in B043, that would let those candidates be compared on physics, or should they be set aside for this year?

Should the committee settle the order of the three leading configurations by resolving the above in sequence (credit boundary for B004, novelty for B006, maturity for B009), or are there combinations, such as a shared prize across subfields, that any member wishes to propose explicitly?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two substantial positions and one minority: four members for B004, three for B006 and one for B009, with the same laureates within each position. The split tracks how members weigh conceptual novelty and breadth of opening support against attribution cleanliness and the overlap with earlier prizes. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap is the most widely shared reservation on B004, and the lineage of the 2005 and 2012 prizes is the most widely shared reservation on B006. As chair I changed my own preference from B002 to B004 after reading the ballots, and my affinity for B043 is disclosed. No ruling is implied by this summary.
